title: Saint Lucia: selected constitutional event
summary: One constitutional commencement event from the Government of Saint Lucia's published legal text supplements the CCP extract, which has no recorded event for this country. This is not a complete constitutional history or a review of later amendments.

sources.title: Government of Saint Lucia: Saint Lucia Constitution Order 1978, sections 1–3

events.title: Independence constitution comes into operation
events.summary: The Constitution Order, made on 20 December 1978, took effect on 22 February 1979. It brought the constitution in Schedule 1 into effect and revoked the 1967 Constitution Order for the associated state.

sources.title: Government of Saint Lucia: Saint Lucia Constitution Order 1978, sections 1–3

mapping_note: This event concerns Saint Lucia's transition from associated-state status. It does not assign earlier British constitutional arrangements to an already independent modern state or imply continuous event coverage after 1979.

title: Palau: selected constitutional event
summary: One constitutional commencement event from the Palau Judiciary's published constitution supplements the CCP extract, which has no recorded event for this country. This is a selected historical event, not a complete amendment chronology.

sources.title: Palau Judiciary: Constitution of the Republic of Palau, Article XV, sections 1–4

events.title: Constitution takes effect
events.summary: Article XV set 1 January 1981 as the constitution's effective date and the installation date for officials elected under it. The transitional provisions separately address the eventual termination of the Trusteeship Agreement.

sources.title: Palau Judiciary: Constitution of the Republic of Palau, Article XV, sections 1–4

mapping_note: The 1981 constitutional commencement is distinct from the later end of trusteeship. Linking this event to PLW is geographic and institutional context, not a claim that Palau was already an independent sovereign state in 1981.

title: Palestine: selected Basic Law events
summary: Two dated Basic Law instruments published by the Palestinian Central Elections Commission supply selected constitutional context outside the CCP extract. They describe legal provisions at those dates, not their subsequent implementation or a complete constitutional history.

sources.title: Palestinian Central Elections Commission: Amended Basic Law, 18 March 2003
Palestinian Central Elections Commission: amendment to the Basic Law, 13 August 2005

events.title: Amended Basic Law promulgated
events.summary: The amended Basic Law was promulgated on 18 March 2003. Its explanatory memorandum describes the creation of a prime minister's office and provisions governing its relationship with the president, cabinet and legislature.

sources.title: Palestinian Central Elections Commission: Amended Basic Law, 18 March 2003

events.title: Basic Law amended on terms of office and elections
events.summary: The amendment promulgated on 13 August 2005 specified four-year presidential and legislative terms, a limit of two consecutive presidential terms, and provisions for legislative elections and transition. Recording the instrument does not establish that those provisions were subsequently implemented.

sources.title: Palestinian Central Elections Commission: amendment to the Basic Law, 13 August 2005

mapping_note: These instruments concern the Palestinian National Authority's governing framework during an expressly interim period. The PSE link does not resolve disputed borders, sovereignty, territorial control or the later operation of Palestinian institutions.

title: San Marino: selected constitutional events
summary: Two selected milestones, described by San Marino's consulate and parliament, supplement a country absent from the CCP extract. The long interval between them is not continuous coverage and does not exhaust San Marino's constitutional sources or later reforms.

sources.title: Consulate of San Marino in the United Kingdom: institutions of the Republic, Statutes of 1600
Grand and General Council of San Marino: Law 59 of 8 July 1974

events.title: Statutes of San Marino promulgated
events.summary: San Marino's consular account dates promulgation of the Leges Statutae Republicae Sancti Marini to 8 October 1600 and identifies them as a source of Sammarinese law. This is an institutional historical account, not a transcription of the original statutes.

sources.title: Consulate of San Marino in the United Kingdom: institutions of the Republic, Statutes of 1600

events.title: Declaration of Citizens' Rights and Fundamental Principles
events.summary: The Grand and General Council's legislative register records the Declaration of Citizens' Rights and the Fundamental Principles of the Sammarinese Legal Order as Law 59 of 8 July 1974.

sources.title: Grand and General Council of San Marino: Law 59 of 8 July 1974

mapping_note: SMR links institutional history to present-day San Marino without projecting present institutions, participation rules or ideology back to 1600. Only the two dated milestones are included; later amendments are outside this supplement.

title: Holy See / Vatican City State: selected constitutional events
summary: Three selected treaty and Fundamental Law events from the Holy See's official legal publications supplement a country absent from the CCP extract. These events concern Vatican City State and are not a complete history of the Holy See or canon law.

sources.title: Holy See Secretariat of State: Lateran Treaty and exchange of ratifications, 1929
Holy See: Fundamental Law of Vatican City State, 13 May 2023, Article 24
Holy See: Fundamental Law of Vatican City State, 31 July 2026, Article 25

events.title: Lateran Treaty establishes Vatican City State
events.summary: The treaty signed on 11 February 1929 provided for Vatican City under the Holy See's sovereignty. It entered into force upon the exchange of ratifications on 7 June 1929.

sources.title: Holy See Secretariat of State: Lateran Treaty, Articles 3 and 27, and exchange of ratifications

events.title: New Fundamental Law enters into force
events.summary: The Fundamental Law issued on 13 May 2023 entered into force on 7 June 2023, replacing the law of 26 November 2000. This records its commencement, not continuing validity through the present.

sources.title: Holy See: Fundamental Law of Vatican City State, 13 May 2023, Article 24

events.title: Fundamental Law replaced in July 2026
events.summary: The Fundamental Law dated 31 July 2026 replaced the 2023 law in its entirety. Article 25 provided for immediate entry into force. This is a dated legal event independently verified outside the CCP dataset's 2025 endpoint.

sources.title: Holy See: Fundamental Law of Vatican City State, 31 July 2026, Article 25

mapping_note: VAT is the ISO registry entry for the Holy See. These records specifically concern Vatican City State's territorial and constitutional framework, whose legal order the Fundamental Laws distinguish from the Roman Curia and other Holy See institutions. They do not assign the historical Papal States to modern Vatican territory.
